sixRiskDetails:
Where rivers can overflow and flood everything.

100-year flood (1% annual exceedance): 19% of land within 12 km flooded, up to 9.2 m deep (p90) · JRC model map, held constant to 2050

Modelled aridity from temperature and rainfall.

30/100 on a custom aridity scale derived from temperature and rainfall (De Martonne). Not a measure of water reserves or drinking-water supply.

Where hot, dry weather can start wildfires.

26/100 on a custom hot/dry-weather proxy. It does not predict actual fires or include local vegetation and ignition.

Where the climate is changing fastest by 2050.

Climate-shift proxy: 23.2/100 · combines temperature and precipitation changes. This is a custom index, not a temperature in °C.

Days too hot to live normally outside.

Estimated 6 days/year above 32 °C heat index · 42 estimated freezing days/year

Where the sea can cover the land.

Supporting snapshot · 2050 (fixed): 0% of land within 12 km below the 2050 flood line · 0% below the line + 1 m · median elevation 87.6 m · line = 2050 level + the 1-in-100-year storm tide (0.00 m, COAST-RP-derived; fallback flags unavailable) · only water connected to the sea counts · earthen dikes are part of the terrain, movable barriers are not · FABDEM relief at 30 m, bare earth
